data.text: `NSpec` is a BDD-style testing framework for .NET. It lets you write specifications using a `describe` / `it` syntax that reads like plain English.
NSpec tests are written in classes that inherit from `nspec`. Use `describe` for the subject and `it` for individual assertions.

data.title: NSpec Example

data.text: NSpec integrates with test runners like NUnit. Run tests from the command line or your IDE.

terms.definition: Groups related specifications about a subject.
Defines a single assertion or expectation.
Runs before each `it` block to set up shared state.

data.title: Tip
data.text: NSpec output reads like living documentation for your codebase.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: NSpec uses `describe` and `it` for BDD-style specs.
Inherit from `nspec` and override lifecycle methods.
Integrates with NUnit for test execution.
data.takeaway: NSpec lets you write readable, behavior-driven tests in .NET.

data.title: Exercise: Write a Calculator Spec
data.description: Write an NSpec specification for a Calculator class.
steps: Create a Calculator class with Add and Subtract methods.
Write an NSpec spec that tests both methods.
Run the tests with dotnet test.
data.expectedOutcome: You can write and run BDD-style specifications with NSpec.
